name: _to_sparse_csr
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_to_sparse_csr(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for every registered overload, keyword argument, return, error, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed to this one signature. All registered schema strings (verbatim): 'aten::_to_sparse_csr(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor' and 'aten::_to_sparse_csr.out(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)'. Semantics derived from the tests: converts a dense tensor of rank >= 2 into sparse CSR layout, treating the two axes ending before the optional dense tail as the sparse matrix axes and any leading axes as batch axes; dense_dim selects the number of trailing dense (hybrid) dimensions and defaults to null (the tests pass the argument omitted, as an explicit null, or as an int in the valid range [0, rank - 2]); the batch axes must have a non-zero product while an empty sparse extent or an empty dense tail converts with the empty extent preserved. The representative 'default' overload returns a single new Tensor and leaves its input unmutated; the registered 'aten::_to_sparse_csr.out' overload is keyword-only 'out', mutates that caller-provided CSR buffer and returns the very same buffer (alias), and is exercised by pytest with nnz/dtype/layout early-check errors. Conditional overload-specific effects are therefore only described here, not modelled in the effect fields. Errors (rank < 2, out-of-range or fractional dense_dim, non-tensor input, zero batch product, invalid out buffer) remain the responsibility of the original pytest. The optional dense_dim default is JSON null, which is an explicit ATen default and not an unresolved value.
